writingReview.title: Editor's review
writingReview.intro: Writing tips to bring your adventure to life. Nothing mandatory: keep what serves your story.
writingReview.allGood: Nothing to report: your campaign avoids the classic pitfalls the review can spot.

WRITE-001-CORRIDOR.observation: "{{entity}}" chains {{count}} scenes without any choice or branch.
WRITE-001-CORRIDOR.why: The players follow a path drawn in advance: they may feel like spectators of the story.
WRITE-001-CORRIDOR.question: At what point could they decide something that changes what happens next?

WRITE-002-FAKE-CHOICE.observation: The {{count}} exits of "{{entity}}" all lead to "{{target}}".
WRITE-002-FAKE-CHOICE.why: When every option ends up in the same place, it's a fake choice, and players eventually notice.
WRITE-002-FAKE-CHOICE.question: What could differ depending on the option chosen: a place, an ally, a price to pay?

WRITE-003-SINGLE-CLUE.observation: The revelation "{{entity}}" is linked from only {{incoming}} scene(s).
WRITE-003-SINGLE-CLUE.why: If the players miss that path, they lose the information and the story stalls. The three clue rule suggests three ways to discover every essential piece of information.
WRITE-003-SINGLE-CLUE.question: In which other scenes could the players find a clue leading there?

WRITE-004-MONOTONOUS-PACING.why: Repetition wears the table out: three fights in a row, or three conversations, end up feeling the same.
WRITE-004-MONOTONOUS-PACING.question: Could a scene of another kind (exploration, conversation, revelation) fit in between?

WRITE-005-NO-STAKES.why: Without stakes, the players don't know why they should act or what they risk: tension drops.
WRITE-005-NO-STAKES.question: What happens if the characters fail, and who suffers?

WRITE-006-LONG-NARRATION.observation: The narration of "{{entity}}" is {{chars}} characters long, more than a minute when read aloud.
WRITE-006-LONG-NARRATION.why: Past one minute, the players' attention drifts and important details get lost.
WRITE-006-LONG-NARRATION.question: What is essential to open the scene, and what can be discovered in play?

WRITE-007-NARRATION-DECIDES.why: The text decides what the characters do or feel. Players like to stay in charge of their reactions.
WRITE-007-NARRATION-DECIDES.question: How could you describe the situation so that they want to react that way on their own?

WRITE-008-COMBAT-NO-PURPOSE.observation: The fight in "{{entity}}" has no described choices and no notes on the enemies' motives.
WRITE-008-COMBAT-NO-PURPOSE.why: A fight with no goal other than taking the enemy down quickly becomes repetitive.
WRITE-008-COMBAT-NO-PURPOSE.question: What do these enemies really want: flee, protect, steal, buy time?

WRITE-009-SINGLE-ENDING.observation: "{{entity}}", the last scene of the arc "{{arc}}", offers no choice and no exit.
WRITE-009-SINGLE-ENDING.why: A single ending written in advance takes the weight out of the players' decisions.
WRITE-009-SINGLE-ENDING.question: What happens if the characters fail, or switch sides?

WRITE-010-UNTYPED-SCENES.observation: {{percent}}% of the campaign's scenes have no type ({{count}} scenes).
WRITE-010-UNTYPED-SCENES.why: Without types, you can't see the adventure's pacing at a glance, and the review can't help you with it.
WRITE-010-UNTYPED-SCENES.question: For each scene: will the players mostly explore, fight, talk, go through an event or discover something?

WRITE-011-ISOLATED-SCENE.observation: "{{entity}}" isn't linked to any other scene: no link leads to it and none leaves it.
WRITE-011-ISOLATED-SCENE.why: In a chapter built with links, an isolated scene is likely never to be played: nothing brings the players there.
WRITE-011-ISOLATED-SCENE.question: From which scene could the players arrive here, and where does this scene lead them next?

WRITE-012-CHOKEPOINT.observation: "{{entity}}" is a chokepoint: every path through the chapter goes through it ({{count}} scene(s) like this).
WRITE-012-CHOKEPOINT.why: If the players fail here, miss the clue or head elsewhere, the story stops. A chokepoint is only a problem if it can be missed.
WRITE-012-CHOKEPOINT.question: What happens if the players fail or bypass this scene? Could another path lead to what comes next?

WRITE-013-LINEAR-DUNGEON.observation: The {{rooms}} rooms of "{{entity}}" follow one another without any loop.
WRITE-013-LINEAR-DUNGEON.why: A place without loops plays like a corridor: a single path, no shortcut, no way to get around an obstacle or escape another way.
WRITE-013-LINEAR-DUNGEON.question: Could two distant rooms be connected (secret passage, duct, hidden stairs) to open a second route?

WRITE-014-NO-PROACTIVE.observation: "{{entity}}" contains revelations but no event scene.
WRITE-014-NO-PROACTIVE.why: When an investigation stalls, the GM needs a scene they can trigger themselves: the enemy strikes back, a witness comes forward, the threat moves on. It restarts play and brings new leads.
WRITE-014-NO-PROACTIVE.question: What does the enemy do if the players go round in circles? Which scene could come to them with a new clue?

WRITE-015-SAME-SOURCE-CLUES.observation: The {{count}} paths leading to "{{entity}}" all start from "{{kind}}" scenes.
WRITE-015-SAME-SOURCE-CLUES.why: If all the information goes through one kind of scene (only interrogations, only searches), a table that dislikes it or fails at it will miss every clue at once.
WRITE-015-SAME-SOURCE-CLUES.question: Could a clue come from another kind of scene: a place to search, a document, an event?

WRITE-016-NPC-NO-MOTIVATION.observation: "{{entity}}" weighs on the plot, but their motivation isn't written.
WRITE-016-NPC-NO-MOTIVATION.why: An opponent or ally who wants nothing specific is hard to play: the GM doesn't know how they react when the players upset their plans.
WRITE-016-NPC-NO-MOTIVATION.question: What does this NPC want, and what are they afraid to lose?

WRITE-017-SINGLE-HOOK.why: If that single reason doesn't speak to the players, the adventure starts reluctantly. Several hooks of different kinds let them choose why to get involved.
WRITE-017-SINGLE-HOOK.question: What other reason, personal or self-interested, could push the characters to act?
